audit.whatIsWrong: Chart said Skill at level 1 where whys[0] plainly states Wukong wins the first exchange, gave Wukong levels 2 and 3 where the whys describe Sylas's burst-heal punishing short trades, and only 'Skill' at level 6 where whys[4] says the Hijack flips the lane. Packet chart reads Wukong, Skill, Skill, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Skill on a 49.4% (801 games) even matchup.
audit.why: Wukong owns level 1 on raw AD and shred before Sylas has W. From 2 through 5 it is close. Level 6 is the one clean Sylas swing because a stolen Cyclone is a knockup he has to answer while his own R is spent.
audit.corrected: Rows realigned to Wukong, Skill, Skill, Skill, Sylas, Skill, Skill in both layers; ratings adjusted on the two rows that changed side meaningfully.

audit.why: Four spikes present: Wukong's level 1, the level 6 Hijacked Cyclone, Riftmaker, and the clone-bait warning. The fourth is a hazard rather than a timing, but it is real content and I did not invent a replacement.

audit.whatIsWrong: Crushing Blow's auto-attack reset is never mentioned. The page also never states that Sylas's E is 13 seconds at rank 1, which is the whole cost of guessing wrong on a clone.
audit.why: The reset is the visual cue that his burst has started — a player watching for the ability cast reacts a beat late and eats the shred. And 'don't hook the clone' means much more when the price is 13 seconds without a gap-closer.
audit.corrected: Crushing Blow named as an auto-reset in the interactions line and in wants.foe[1]; the 13-second E cooldown written into whys[1].

audit.why: All five Wukong ability names on the page (Crushing Blow, Warrior Trickster referenced as the W clone, Nimbus Strike, Cyclone) match the packet's ability list, and the packet reported no suspect names or defects.

edits.before: Track Wukong’s Nimbus Strike: His only gap-close — he cannot reach you while it is down. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Nimbus Strike, his only gap-close, and Crushing Blow — it is an auto-attack reset, so step off on the wind-up, not on the cast.

edits.before: W online means your burst-heal now punishes his short trades; take controlled exchanges but respect his clone juke before committing E2.
edits.after: W online means your burst-heal punishes his short trades; take controlled exchanges, but E is 13s down if a clone eats it — confirm the real one first.

edits.before: Q armor-shred before every extended trade so his autos and Cyclone damage compound against your lower effective HP
edits.after: Open with a Crushing Blow auto-reset so the shred lands before you react, then compound autos on your lower effective HP

notes: The brief's enemyKit for Wukong is null — no Data Dragon entry was supplied — so I had no authority for his cooldowns, ranges or ability text and did not correct or invent any. Ability names were checked against packet.enemyAbilities and all five on the page are correct. Three existing claims are plausible but unverified from the data I had and were therefore left untouched: that the decoy runs in a straight line and never casts abilities, that Wukong cannot Warrior Trickster out of Cyclone once the spin is active, and the Black Cleaver / armour-stacking build assumptions. They are listed in unverified.
